name: Macbeth 1.7: "We will proceed no further"
play: Macbeth, Act 1 Scene 7 (Shakespeare, public domain): Macbeth wavers, Lady Macbeth shames him, he gives in.

from.shape: two people seated facing each other; a wide shot, a single on one, over her shoulder onto the other, closer on the first

shots.note: Wide: Macbeth walks in, stops, turns his back to his chair and sits down, and says it as he sits.
shots.why: Mixamo transitions chained by perform.py (go): start walking, walk, stop walking, a right turn on the spot, stand to sit backing into his chair, then sitting still; each at its own pace, joins blended

shots.note: Over her shoulder onto Macbeth as he refuses.
shots.why: over her shoulder onto Macbeth as he refuses ('Prithee, peace'); no added turn: his own seated build, which reads as natural
the same shot as he asks 'If we should fail?'; his build from 4.6 s, ending before its last frame (that frame turns the body 30 degrees)

shots.note: Closer on Lady Macbeth: she turns in on him.
shots.why: closer on Lady Macbeth: she turns in on him for 'screw your courage'; her build slower and back and forth

shots.note: Back on Macbeth for his answer.
shots.why: back on Macbeth for his answer; Lady Macbeth holds the last pose of her shot 5 build, her back to us, still turned in

shots.note: Wide: Macbeth stands, turns away and walks out.
shots.why: Mixamo sit to stand, a right turn on the spot toward the way out, start walking and walk off (perform.py rise); the way out passes 0.7 m clear of the candle stand

lines.text: We will proceed no further in this business.
Was the hope drunk wherein you dressed yourself?
Prithee, peace. I dare do all that may become a man; who dares do more is none.
We fail? But screw your courage to the sticking-place, and we'll not fail.
Away, and mock the time with fairest show: false face must hide what the false heart doth know.

set.note: on Macbeth's side, toward the wide camera: in the wide shot only, out of the close shots
the wine she drugged the grooms with, on the stool

card: Hand-written for now. A seated two-person scene of pressure and giving in: one argues, the other refuses, wavers and is won over. Shape from the source: a wide two-shot, a single on the persuader, over her shoulder onto the doubter, closer on the persuader, back to the doubter. Performed as Macbeth 1.7 in a castle room: chairs, a candle stand, a stool with a chalice, banners. Blocking from the text: Macbeth walks in and sits; at the end he stands and walks out; Macbeth turns away on 'Prithee, peace' and back on 'If we should fail?'; Lady Macbeth turns in on him for 'screw your courage'. Good for: confession, interrogation, a deal won by pressure, a parent talking a child round. Not for: walking, standing, contact.
